A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PSC research work despite the changed title and format. Their complete main texts, appendices, algorithms and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original ImageNet compression experiments, MSCOCO latent-PSC examples, caption comparisons and measurement-rank analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains original experimental results and adds CLIC/DIV2K compression evaluations and comparisons with additional codecs.

M1.justification: The adaptive PCA transform, synchronized encoder/decoder, float8 quantization and range coding remain. Appendix A changes latent-PSC's projected-DDPM sampling and PiGDM restoration to DDRM sampling and Nested Diffusion restoration, a limited procedural revision within the existing framework.

E1.justification: V3 adds CLIC and DIV2K validation images for quantitative natural-image compression evaluation, plus a Kodak example. ImageNet and MSCOCO remain; the MSCOCO experiments move to Appendix D. This substantially broadens the evaluated data beyond v2's ImageNet evaluation and MSCOCO demonstrations.

E2.justification: The ImageNet comparison adds ELIC, IPIC and MS-ILLM to JPEG, JPEG2000, BPG and HiFiC (v2 Figure 2 versus v3 Figure 5). V3 also evaluates latent-PSC against PerCo, MS-ILLM and BPG, whereas v2's latent experiments lacked competing-codec comparisons.

E3.justification: V3 introduces PSNR/KID evaluation on 512×512 CLIC/DIV2K validation images, using 64×64 patches for KID and reporting matched PerCo components. Latent sampling changes from 25 projected-DDPM steps to 50 DDRM steps; restoration uses 50 Nested Diffusion outer steps with five inner steps instead of 100-step PiGDM. The ImageNet evaluation protocol remains.

E4.justification: V2's four image-specific rate–distortion curves are removed (Appendix D, Figure 8). V3 adds a posterior-mean and posterior-sample progression case study across bit-rates (Figure 10). The measurement-rank and caption ablations retain their results, making this a limited revision of supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run performance uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Shared seeds coordinate the encoder and decoder in both versions; posterior sample counts describe algorithm operation rather than repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: V3 adds CLIC/DIV2K PSNR/KID curves, results for new ImageNet comparators and additional latent-codec examples (Figures 1, 5, 6 and 9). Retained ImageNet curve points, qualitative examples, rank results and MSCOCO results match. The individual-image curves disappear. New latent results use revised settings and do not establish a same-setting improvement over v2.

T1.justification: The linear measurement setup, PCA/SVD row-selection rule and progressive transform construction remain mathematically unchanged. V3 expands the background and synchronization explanations without introducing a new formal theorem, proof or derivation; v2's block-append equation remains represented by the algorithmic operations.

C1.justification: The core zero-shot, progressive, image-adaptive compression contribution remains. V3 softens the introduction's superiority claims to competitiveness and explicitly emphasizes instance-level rate/distortion control and applicability to any data type supported by a diffusion model.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies row-selection optimality through linear-decoder MSE, uses the existing VAE-related PSNR limitation to motivate latent-PSC's perceptual focus, and interprets MS-ILLM's distortion advantage accordingly. It also adds nonlinear measurement-optimization complexity to the limitations. The principal computational and quantization limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds an approximately 10,000-function-evaluation cost disclosure, latent float16 precision, baseline implementation sources and a decoder measurement-slice correction. Reproducibility remains imperfect: Appendix A names Stable Diffusion 2.1-base but links to 2-base, and replaces explicit latent sample/rank counts with 'same hyperparameters.' Complete code remains promised upon acceptance.

R1.justification: V3 adds positioning against IPIC's perceptual decoding and Gao et al.'s post-hoc rate reconfiguration, alongside references for Nested Diffusion, new baselines, datasets and KID. The central relationship to AdaSense and distinction from training-based compression remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Background becomes three subsections, implementation choices and latent-PSC gain dedicated subsections, limitations and conclusion are merged, and appendix sections are reordered. These are substantial editorial and structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column main-text layout, separates encoder and decoder algorithm displays, and adds mechanism, comparison and progression figures. Existing diagrams and MSCOCO examples move to appendices; plotting ranges, legends and styling change, and the rank plots change from a grid to a horizontal arrangement. The individual-image curve figure is removed.

improvement.justification: V2 supported latent-PSC primarily with qualitative examples. V3 supplies quantitative comparisons against relevant codecs on CLIC and DIV2K, expands ImageNet baselines, and moderates superiority claims to competitiveness. This substantially strengthens the empirical support for a central part of the paper. Clearer exposition also helps; these gains outweigh the removed individual-image analysis and remaining checkpoint/hyperparameter ambiguity.
